person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The findings of the SLR indicate that AI approach used in mathematics education for the samples studied were through robotics, systems, tools, teachable agent, autonomous agent, and a comprehensive approach.

span.label: artificial intelligence in mathematics education
span.quote: The goal of this review is to add to the conversation by offering a complete overview of AI in mathematics teaching and learning for students at all levels of education.

span.label: systematic-review
span.quote: A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted using established and robust guidelines.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the high maintenance cost of AI equipment restricts who can run such studies, which is why the reviewed research clusters in developed countries and is absent from Southeast Asia
span.quote: Meanwhile, AI is also difficult to apply comprehensively due to relatively high maintenance costs. Therefore, it is believed that this was why many studies were only conducted in developed countries such as the United States, China, and Australia while zero studies in Southeast Asia, especially in Malaysia.

span.label: Only a small number of eligible articles exist, so broad conclusions cannot be drawn
span.quote: The first limitation is that only a limited number of articles are available for research.

span.label: AI is rarely investigated in mathematics education, limiting the results obtained
span.quote: Because AI is a topic that is rarely investigated in mathematics education, the results gained are limited, making it difficult to draw broad conclusions from the findings.

span.label: De-duplication across search engines reduced the number of relevant studies acquired
span.quote: As previously stated, AI topics have a limited number of studies; therefore, eliminating duplicate articles amongst search engines decreases the acquisition of relevant research studies.

span.label: Only journal articles were included; proceedings and books were excluded
span.quote: Since the studies included in the analysis focused exclusively on journal articles, future research should consider using conference proceedings and books to enhance the findings and analysis.

span.label: The review's central term is stated to have no agreed definition, and the review adopts none.
span.quote: To date, there are diverse concept of AI in the current literature. The problem in defining AI, known as machine intelligence (Poole et al., 1998), is to define artificiality’s parameters, or the manners in which computers differ from human intelligence

span.label: The population is defined by a list of search synonyms rather than by a concept.
span.quote: Synonyms and alternatives terms for main search terms Artificial intelligence AI Robotics Machine learning Neural networks Fuzzy logic Natural language processing Expert systems

span.label: The three article counts printed for the search stage are inconsistent with each other.
span.quote: 864 results were identified using search strategies, while additional papers (n=20) were identified from other sources. As a result, a total of 885 journal articles had been classified at this stage

span.label: The corpus is restricted by language and by a five-year window.
span.quote: we were only concentrating on English-language journal articles made it less likely that complex or uncertain translations would be required. Then, we looked at articles published within the previous five years (between 2017 and 2021)

span.label: A PROCEDURAL SAFEGUARD ON A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW: every one of the 845 articles read through title, abstract, methodology, results and discussion against the stated selection criteria, rather than screened on title and abstract alone
span.quote: to ensure that all 845 articles fit the study’s selection criteria and objectives, each article’s title, abstract, methodology, results, and discussion were thoroughly reviewed

span.label: artificial intelligence
span.quote: Synonyms and alternatives terms for main search terms Artificial intelligence AI Robotics Machine learning Neural networks Fuzzy logic Natural language processing Expert systems

span.label: machine intelligence
span.quote: The problem in defining AI, known as machine intelligence (Poole et al., 1998), is to define artificiality’s parameters, or the manners in which computers differ from human intelligence

span.label: expert systems
span.quote: Synonyms and alternatives terms for main search terms Artificial intelligence AI Robotics Machine learning Neural networks Fuzzy logic Natural language processing Expert systems

span.label: intelligent tutoring system
span.quote: An intelligent tutoring system (Hasanein & Abu-Naser, 2018) is a computer program designed to simulate the behavior and guidance of a human teacher

span.label: computer program
span.quote: An intelligent tutoring system (Hasanein & Abu-Naser, 2018) is a computer program designed to simulate the behavior and guidance of a human teacher

span.label: AI - THREE CHARACTERISATIONS AND NO RULING: the review reports that there are diverse concepts of AI in the literature and that defining it is a problem, then quotes a confluence of technologies, computers that do cognitive functions, and a process that produces human intelligence through machines - three sources, one review, and no statement of which the review is using
span.quote: To date, there are diverse concept of AI in the current literature. The problem in defining AI, known as machine intelligence (Poole et al., 1998), is to define artificiality’s parameters, or the manners in which computers differ from human intelligence

span.label: AI, OPERATIONALLY - A LIST OF EIGHT SEARCH STRINGS: what the review actually counts is papers matching artificial intelligence, AI, robotics, machine learning, neural networks, fuzzy logic, natural language processing or expert systems, so a table of search synonyms is doing the work that none of the three definitions does
span.quote: Synonyms and alternatives terms for main search terms Artificial intelligence AI Robotics Machine learning Neural networks Fuzzy logic Natural language processing Expert systems

span.label: machine intelligence - THE ALTERNATIVE NAME, GIVEN IN PASSING: the review introduces the problem of defining AI as the problem of defining artificiality's parameters, and names the field 'machine intelligence' in the same clause, attributing it to Poole et al. 1998
span.quote: The problem in defining AI, known as machine intelligence (Poole et al., 1998), is to define artificiality’s parameters, or the manners in which computers differ from human intelligence

span.label: builds-on → Ouyang and Jiao (2021) conceptual framework of AI-directed / AI-supported / AI-empowered learning
span.quote: Therefore, in the current work, we follow the idea of Ouyang and Jiao (2021) as conceptual framework namely AI-directed (learner-as-recipient), AI-supported (learner-as-collaborator), and AI-empowered 9 learner-as-leader).

span.label: builds-on → Moher et al. (2009) PRISMA flow diagram
span.quote: Figure 2 displays the PRISMA flow chart in this study adapted and modified from Moher et al. (2009).

span.label: replicates → Zhong and Xia (2020) systematic review of robotics in mathematics learning
span.quote: The result was in line with Zhong and Xia (2020) who conducted a systematic review that stated that there is a potential for future research and the rapid development of evidence-based research on teaching and learning mathematical content knowledge through robotics.

span.label: intelligent tutoring system —is-a→ computer program
span.quote: An intelligent tutoring system (Hasanein & Abu-Naser, 2018) is a computer program designed to simulate the behavior and guidance of a human teacher

span.label: Robotics was the most common AI approach in the 20 reviewed mathematics-education studies, accounting for 45% (n=9) of them.
span.quote: As seen in Figure 3, the majority of AI approach used for the samples studied were through robotics (45%, n=9)

span.label: The USA and Mexico produced the largest share of the reviewed studies, three each.
span.quote: It can be shown that the majority of the collected studies (n=3) were carried out in the USA

span.label: Quantitative designs were the most used methodology among the reviewed studies, at 40% (n=8).
span.quote: The analysis revealed that most of the studies reviewed (40%, n=8) used quantitative research methods

span.label: 2021 was the peak publication year for AI-in-mathematics-education articles in the review window, with 30% of the corpus.
span.quote: In 2021 the percentage number of articles published on AI is the highest compared to other years (30%)

span.label: Effectiveness of AI was the most studied theme, appearing in 60% (n=12) of the reviewed papers, far ahead of strategies, idea suggestion, factors, role and conceptual understanding.
span.quote: As seen in Figure 7, the most studied theme (60%, n=12) was about effectiveness

span.label: Of the 845 articles carried into the eligibility stage, 834 were rejected for not fully explaining AI in mathematics education or not clearly reporting findings, leaving 20 studies.
span.quote: At this point, 834 articles have been rejected because they do not fully explain AI in mathematics education or do not clearly explain and review the findings data in the study findings section.

span.label: artificial intelligence (AI)
span.quote: AI is a process that produces human intelligence through machines, especially computer systems.

span.label: systematic literature review (SLR)
span.quote: SLR is a method of gathering appropriate data on a certain topic that meets pre-determined eligibility criteria (Mengist et al., 2020).

span.label: PRISMA
span.quote: PRISMA is based on four steps: identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion.

span.label: intelligent tutoring system
span.quote: An intelligent tutoring system (Hasanein & Abu-Naser, 2018) is a computer program designed to simulate the behavior and guidance of a human teacher

span.label: research methodology
span.quote: A research methodology is a specific process or approach for identifying, selecting, processing, and analyzing information about a specific topic.

span.label: publication window (2017-2021)
span.quote: This study only looked at journal publications published between 2017 and 2021; no older articles were included.

span.label: publication language (English only)
span.quote: And, we were only concentrating on English-language journal articles made it less likely that complex or uncertain translations would be required.

span.label: 45%, n=9 — share of reviewed studies using a robotics approach to AI
span.quote: As seen in Figure 3, the majority of AI approach used for the samples studied were through robotics (45%, n=9)

span.label: 40%, n=8 — share of reviewed studies using quantitative methods
span.quote: The analysis revealed that most of the studies reviewed (40%, n=8) used quantitative research methods

span.label: 60%, n=12 — share of reviewed studies whose theme was effectiveness of AI
span.quote: As seen in Figure 7, the most studied theme (60%, n=12) was about effectiveness

span.label: 30% — share of the reviewed corpus published in 2021, the peak year
span.quote: In 2021 the percentage number of articles published on AI is the highest compared to other years (30%)

span.label: 864 — records retrieved by the database searches, plus 20 from other sources
span.quote: Through ProQuest, EBSCOHost, ScienceDirect, Springer, Scopus, 864 results were identified using search strategies, while additional papers (n=20) were identified from other sources.

span.label: 834 — articles rejected at the eligibility stage
span.quote: At this point, 834 articles have been rejected because they do not fully explain AI in mathematics education or do not clearly explain and review the findings data in the study findings section.

span.label: 20 — articles retained for the final synthesis
span.quote: As a result, 20 articles were selected for publication in the final stage of the review process (see Figure 1).
